epithet: “Has he made the gods into one God?”
lede: The chiefs of Quraysh went to Abū Ṭālib’s sickbed to settle things with his nephew, were asked for one sentence, and walked out. The surah records what they said as they left — and then tells of three servants who were tested with power, with kingship and with pain, and each time turned back to their Lord.

names.name: Ṣād
names.note: The single letter it opens with.

names.name: Dāwūd
names.note: A name Ibn al-Jawzī records, after the prophet whose story it tells first and at greatest length.

revelation.detail: It is Makkan in the saying of all. Its opening is tied to a meeting between the chiefs of Quraysh and Abū Ṭālib, which the reports place in his last illness — so in the later Makkan years. The traditional order places it thirty-eighth.
revelation.when: Makkah, in the lifetime of Abū Ṭālib — the reports say, in his last illness

evidence.quote: سُورَةُ صَ وَيُقالُ لَها: سُورَةُ داوُدَ، وهي مَكِّيَّةٌ [كُلُّها] بِإجْماعِهِمْ
سُورَةُ ص مَكِّيَّةٌ فِي قَوْلِ الْجَمِيعِ

setting: Ibn ʿAbbās relates the occasion. Quraysh complained of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ to his uncle and protector, Abū Ṭālib. He sent for him: “Nephew, what do you want of your people?” He said: “Uncle, I want from them only one word, by which the Arabs will yield to them and the non-Arabs pay them tribute.” “One word?” “One word.” “What is it?” “Lā ilāha illā Allāh.” They got up, shaking out their robes: “Has he made the gods into one God? This is an astonishing thing.” And the opening of the surah came down about them.

The surah quotes them further. Their leaders set off saying, “Go on, and stand by your gods — this is something that is being plotted. We never heard of this in the latest religion. It is nothing but an invention. Has the Reminder been sent down to him, out of all of us?” The last question is the truest. What they could not bear was that revelation should have come to him and not to one of them.

To the one who had to listen to this, the surah says: “Be patient with what they say, and remember Our servant Dāwūd.” Three prophets follow, each given something immense and each tried in it. Dāwūd was given strength, a kingdom and judgement; he was tested, understood at once, and fell down in prostration. Sulaymān was given a dominion such as no one after him would have; he was tested, and turned back. Ayyūb was given affliction, and called on his Lord — “and We found him patient: an excellent servant, ever turning back.” The same praise is given to all three.

Of Dāwūd’s trial, Ibn Kathīr writes that the commentators relate a story most of which is taken from Israelite sources, that nothing binding is established about it from the Prophet ﷺ, and that the right course is to keep to what the Qurʾan itself recites.
The surah ends at the beginning of the human story: the creation of Ādam, and the one who would not bow.

occasions.title: One word
occasions.text: Quraysh complained of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ to Abū Ṭālib. He asked him what he wanted of his people, and he said: “I want from them a single word, by which the Arabs will submit to them and the non-Arabs pay them the jizyah: lā ilāha illā Allāh.” They said: “Has he made the gods one God?” And there came down about them: “Ṣād. By the Qurʾan, full of reminder…” to “this is nothing but an invention.”
occasions.source: Ibn ʿAbbās: Aḥmad and al-Tirmidhī (3232), who graded it ḥasan; al-Albānī judged its chain weak.

evidence.quote: أنَّ قُرَيْشًا شَكَوا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ ﷺ إلى أبِي طالِبٍ، فَقالَ: يا ابْنَ أخِي، ما تُرِيدُ مِن قَوْمِكَ؟ فَقالَ: "يا عَمِّ، إنَّما أُرِيدُ مِنهم كَلِمَةً تَذِلُّ لَهم بِها العَرَبُ وتُؤَدِّي إلَيْهِمُ الجِزْيَةَ بِها العَجَمُ

occasions.title: On Dāwūd’s trial
occasions.text: Ibn Kathīr declines to relate the stories told about what Dāwūd’s trial was: most of them are drawn from Israelite reports, and nothing that must be followed is established about it from the Prophet ﷺ. It is better, he says, to confine oneself to reciting the account as it stands, and to refer its knowledge to Allah.

evidence.quote: قَدْ ذَكَرَ الْمُفَسِّرُونَ هَاهُنَا قِصَّةً أَكْثَرُهَا مَأْخُوذٌ مِنَ الْإِسْرَائِيلِيَّاتِ وَلَمْ يَثْبُتْ فِيهَا عَنِ الْمَعْصُومِ حَدِيثٌ يَجِبُ اتِّبَاعُهُ

aim: To recount contention in the cause of falsehood, and what it leads to.
themes: The quarrel of the people of the Fire

outline.title: Their astonishment
outline.summary: Ṣād. By the Qurʾan, full of reminder: those who disbelieve are sunk in pride and dissent. They marvel that a warner has come to them from among themselves, and say: “A sorcerer, a liar. Has he made the gods one God?” Their chiefs go off: “Stand by your gods.” Before them the people of Nūḥ denied, and ʿĀd, and Pharaoh of the stakes, and Thamūd, the people of Lūṭ and the people of the Thicket. They say, “Our Lord, hasten our share to us before the Day of Reckoning.”

outline.title: Dāwūd
outline.summary: Be patient with what they say, and remember Our servant Dāwūd, the man of strength, ever turning back. The mountains and the birds glorified with him. Two disputants climbed into his sanctuary: one had ninety-nine ewes and the other one. Dāwūd understood that We had tried him; he asked his Lord’s forgiveness, fell down bowing, and turned back. “Dāwūd, We have made you a vicegerent on the earth: so judge between people in truth, and do not follow desire.” A blessed Book We have sent down to you, that they may ponder its ayat.

outline.title: Sulaymān
outline.summary: To Dāwūd We gave Sulaymān — an excellent servant, ever turning back. The fine horses were shown to him at evening. We tried Sulaymān, and placed a body on his throne; then he turned back and said: “My Lord, forgive me, and grant me a kingdom that will befit no one after me.” So We subjected the wind to him, and the devils — every builder and diver.

outline.title: Ayyūb, and the others
outline.summary: Remember Our servant Ayyūb, when he called to his Lord: “Satan has afflicted me with hardship and pain.” “Strike with your foot: here is a cool bath, and drink.” We gave him back his family and their like with them. We found him patient: an excellent servant, ever turning back. And remember Ibrāhīm, Isḥāq and Yaʿqūb, men of strength and vision; and Ismāʿīl, al-Yasaʿ and Dhū l-Kifl — all among the best.

outline.title: Two destinations
outline.summary: For the mindful there is a good return: Gardens of Eden, their gates opened for them. For the transgressors an evil return: Hell. There they turn on one another — “No welcome to them!” — “No, no welcome to you!” — and ask, “Why do we not see men we used to count among the wicked?” That is the truth: the wrangling of the people of the Fire.

outline.title: Ādam and Iblīs
outline.summary: Say: I am only a warner, and there is no god but Allah, the One, the Subduer. When your Lord said to the angels, “I am creating a human being from clay; when I have shaped him and breathed into him of My spirit, fall down before him in prostration,” they did, all together — except Iblīs. “What prevented you from prostrating to what I created with My two hands?” — “I am better than him.” — “Then leave; you are accursed.” He swore to mislead them all, except Your chosen servants. Say: I ask of you no wage for it. It is only a reminder to the worlds — and you will come to know its news after a time.

keyAyah.why: Why the Book was sent down: to be pondered. The surah places it straight after Dāwūd is told to judge by the truth and not by desire.

virtues.text: Ibn ʿAbbās said: “Ṣād is not among the obligatory prostrations — but I saw the Prophet ﷺ prostrate at it.” And when Mujāhid asked him on what basis he prostrated there, he recited: “‘And of his descendants, Dāwūd and Sulaymān… those are the ones Allah guided, so follow their guidance.’ Dāwūd was among those your Prophet was commanded to follow. Dāwūd prostrated at it, so the Messenger of Allah ﷺ prostrated at it.”

before: Al-Ṣāffāt recalled the idolaters saying, “Shall we leave our gods for a mad poet?” Ṣād opens with the scene in which they said it to his face, and left.
after: Ṣād closes: it is only a reminder to the worlds. Al-Zumar opens: the sending down of the Book is from Allah — so worship Him, making the religion His alone.

notable.label: “Has he made the gods one God?”
Dāwūd fell down bowing — an ayah of prostration
A blessed Book, that they may ponder its ayat
